title: Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion
abstract: We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $β_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leqρ_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $ρ_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $δ\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $δ^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $δ$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.
summary: This paper presents advanced algorithms to approximate the partition function of mixed $p$-spin glass models, including the SK model, in weak external fields. It achieves logarithmic accuracy using sophisticated techniques like cluster expansions and reverse hypercontractivity. The work provides polynomial-time complexity guarantees for this difficult counting problem in statistical physics.
main_problem: The paper develops algorithms to approximate the partition function of mixed $p$-spin glass models, including the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model, in the presence of weak external fields.
main_result: The authors provide algorithms that can approximate $\log Z_N$ to an additive error $\epsilon$ with a failure probability bounded by $\delta + 	au_N$, achieving this with a cost polynomial in $N$, $\epsilon^{-1}$, and $\delta^{-1}$.
method: The core method involves using cluster expansions, building upon techniques from Aizenman–Lebowitz–Ruelle, and employing advanced tools like randomized color coding and reverse hypercontractivity to control error terms.
model_or_system: The system studied is the mixed $p$-spin glass model, characterized by a Hamiltonian involving interactions of order $p \ge 3$. The analysis is performed for the SK model and generalized to mixed $p$-spin interactions.
key_observables: The primary observable is the partition function, $Z_N$, and its logarithm, $\log Z_N$. The approximation targets $\log b_{ZN}$, where $b_{ZN}$ is a normalized version of $Z_N$.
important_parameters: The analysis is valid in the weak external field regime $|h| \le ho_0 N^{-1/4}$ and below the second-moment threshold $ eta_f$. The complexity depends on the desired accuracy $\epsilon$ and failure probability $\delta$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the existence of finite moments (e.g., finite fourth moment for the disorder) and the successful application of reverse hypercontractivity to convert mean-square error bounds into logarithmic accuracy.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the approximation by first establishing bounds using cluster expansions, then refining the error control using techniques like inclusion-exclusion and color coding for specific models (SK), and finally deriving the main algorithmic result with explicit complexity bounds.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques developed for approximating partition functions in complex, disordered systems are highly relevant to understanding the phase transitions and ground states of quantum spin models, which often map onto spin glass physics.
